subject: Mixed-path partial degradation during partner transit maintenance - attribution question
messages:
From: Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@cloudmosaic.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cloudmosaic.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial path degradation during our scheduled transit maintenance (Mar 21)

Irene —

Quick note from our ops team: on Mar 21 between 02:14 and 02:29 UTC we performed a planned transit window on our east-west backbone. During that 15-min maintenance you should see elevated packet loss on a handful of TTL-hopped paths; we've attached our MTR export and timestamps.

Per our contract, that maintenance should be treated as an excluded event. We're seeing Redwood's uptime ledger still counting ~9 minutes of error budget as customer-visible for our account, and we'd like that re-evaluated.

Attachments: transit-mtr-20280321.txt (attachment)

Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful — Kyle
Kyle Turner
Sr. Network Ops, CloudMosaic
kyle.turner@cloudmosaic.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@cloudmosaic.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial path degradation during our scheduled transit maintenance (Mar 21)

Kyle —

Thanks for the MTR — we received it. I'm looping in Jonas and Sergio from SRE/Telemetry so we can compare probe visibility. Two quick asks to help expedite:

1) Can CloudMosaic confirm the exact ASN prefix range for the transit change? That helps match our probe mapping.
2) Any topology change notes (BGP communities withdrawn/announced) during the 02:14–02:29 UTC window?

We're going to pull probe logs on our side and will share a short trace. If this is fully within your scheduled maintenance window and traffic was intentionally blackholed, we can mark the corresponding observed impact as third-party excluded. The complication: some traces show mixed-path behavior where only a subset of our probe set saw impact while other probes rerouted through Redwood-controlled infrastructure, which affects apportionment.

Irene Choi
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@cloudmosaic.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial path degradation during our scheduled transit maintenance (Mar 21)

Irene/Kyle —

I pulled the probe ledger for that window and attached a condensed CSV showing per-probe loss and which egress POPs were implicated. Summary:
- 12 probes targeted at customer edges showed >50% loss for a 9 minute contiguous span.
- 28 probes saw minimal loss (<1%) due to alternate peering paths.
- The affected probes mapped to two Redwood POPs (iad1-edge, ord1-edge) and one transit hop that corresponds with CloudMosaic ASN 64512 (per our AS mapping).

Because this is a mixed-path, partial-degradation event (not full-region outage), our standard apportionment method is to allocate credits proportionally to affected probe weight. That said, if CloudMosaic provides BGP withdraw/announce timestamps and a canonical ASN prefix list, we can try to exclude the portion strictly within CloudMosaic's transit behavior.

Attached: probe_loss_summary_20280321.csv (attachment), redwood-uptime-ledger-20271121.csv (attachment)

On Fri, Mar 29, 2028 at 09:12 AM Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@cloudmosaic.com> wrote:
> Irene —
>
> Quick note from our ops team: on Mar 21 between 02:14 and 02:29 UTC we performed a planned transit window on our east-west backbone...

Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@cloudmosaic.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 07:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial path degradation during our scheduled transit maintenance (Mar 21)

Jonas —

Thanks for the summary. Per your request: attached is the ASN prefix list and BGP timeline (withdraw at 02:14:12 UTC, reannounce at 02:29:07 UTC). Our ops asserts that any customer-visible loss within that exact interval should be excluded.

However, note two things:
1) We observed some transient blackholing that only impacted peering into iad1-edge — ord1-edge traffic. Traffic that rerouted via a different transit partner did not see loss.
2) CloudMosaic's maintenance announcement was sent through the portal and via the registered escalation channel.

Attachments: cloudmosaic-asn-prefixes.csv (attachment), bgp-timeline-20280321.log (attachment)

If Redwood still sees a remainder of counted degraded minutes after strict exclusion, please propose a split so we can agree on apportionment.

–Kyle

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@cloudmosaic.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial path degradation during our scheduled transit maintenance (Mar 21)

Kyle —

Appreciate the timely evidence. We're close but not aligned on the ledger delta. Here's our proposed approach to close this without a formal dispute:

- Exclude all probe minutes that map 1:1 to CloudMosaic ASN withdraw/reannounce intervals (strict exclusion).
- For remaining impacted probe-minutes where rerouting caused partial customer impact, apply a proportional apportionment where CloudMosaic covers 70% of those minutes and Redwood covers 30% to account for internal dependency (radial peering fallbacks we control).

This split reflects that many customer transactions experienced increased tail latency even when loss wasn't absolute; our internal routing decisions during the maintenance mitigated broader impact but did not fully prevent increased error surface. If you accept, we'll issue a credit corresponding to the excluded minutes + 70% of the apportioned minutes.

If CloudMosaic prefers a tight reprocessing based strictly on ASN-only mapping (100% exclude when ASN matches), we can run that and share the delta, but it may take 48–72 hours.

Please confirm preference and we'll proceed.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@cloudmosaic.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial path degradation during our scheduled transit maintenance (Mar 21)

Marissa —

Thanks for the concrete proposal. We prefer the ASN-only strict exclusion, please run the reprocessing and share the delta. If the delta still shows material residual minutes, we will revisit a split, but we'd like the canonical mapping first.

I'll expect the reprocessed ledger link or summary within 72 hours. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Kyle Turner
Sr. Network Ops, CloudMosaic
